node_kinds.title: Start
node_kinds.description: Where the main line begins. Exactly one per graph.

node_kinds.title: End
node_kinds.description: Ends the run. Whatever reaches `result` is the run's answer.

node_kinds.title: Model
node_kinds.description: An endpoint plus a model name. Feed it into the agents that should run on it; agents with no model wired run on the session's own.

fields.name: api_mode
fields.label: API mode
fields.help: Empty follows the session setting.

fields.name: base_url
fields.label: Base URL
fields.help: Empty follows the session setting.

fields.name: api_key_ref
fields.label: API key
fields.help: session (use the session key), env:NAME, or secret:NAME. A literal key is refused - this file goes into git.

fields.name: reasoning_effort
fields.label: Reasoning effort
fields.help: Empty follows the session; none turns thinking off.

node_kinds.title: Agent
node_kinds.description: One isolated agent running one task to a report. You decide who it is (a profession, or your own instructions) and what it may touch (the switches, or Tools nodes wired into `tools`).

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: What to call it on the node and in the log. Empty uses the profession.

fields.name: profession
fields.label: Profession
fields.help: A ready-made role and toolbox. Custom means you write the role under Instructions. Ignored while a Profession node is wired in.

fields.name: role_override
fields.label: Instructions
fields.help: Custom: who this agent is and how it works. With a profession: added to its role.

fields.name: blocked_tools
fields.label: Never use
fields.help: Taken away whatever the switches or the wired Tools nodes allow.

fields.name: max_steps
fields.label: Max steps
fields.help: 0 keeps the profession's budget.

fields.name: timeout_s
fields.label: Timeout (s)
fields.help: 0 keeps the profession's budget.

node_kinds.title: Profession
node_kinds.description: A job description you write once: the role prompt is the job, the switches are what it may touch. Wire it into the profession pin of every Agent that shares the job.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: What to call it. Shows on the node and in the run log.

fields.name: role
fields.label: Role
fields.help: Who this agent is and how it works - the same voice as the built-in professions. It is the whole job description.

fields.name: framing
fields.label: Add workspace framing
fields.help: Off, the role text is the entire system prompt. On, the usual sub-agent preamble is added: workspace path, rules, report-back instructions. Leave it off for agents that talk to each other.

fields.name: blocked_tools
fields.label: Never use
fields.help: Taken away whatever the switches or the wired Tools nodes allow.

fields.name: max_steps
fields.label: Max steps
fields.help: How many tool round-trips it gets before it must report.

fields.name: timeout_s
fields.label: Timeout (s)
fields.help: 0 keeps the worker budget from settings.

node_kinds.title: Clean agent
node_kinds.description: Sends the task to the model as it is: no system prompt unless you write one, no framing, no tools, nothing added. The reply is the report.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: What to call it on the node and in the log.

fields.name: system
fields.label: System prompt
fields.help: Sent exactly as written. Empty sends no system message at all.

fields.name: timeout_s
fields.label: Timeout (s)
fields.help: 0 keeps the worker budget from settings.

node_kinds.title: Tools
node_kinds.description: A hand-picked set of tools. Wire it into an Agent's tools pin and the agent gets exactly these; wire several and they add up.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: Shows on the node, e.g. 'read-only' or 'git'.

node_kinds.title: Sequence
node_kinds.description: Runs each output in order, waiting for one branch to finish before the next.

node_kinds.title: Decision
node_kinds.description: Two ways forward. `bool` reads a wired condition; `judge` asks a model a yes/no question about the run so far.

fields.name: prompt
fields.label: Question
fields.help: Answerable with yes or no.

node_kinds.title: Loop
node_kinds.description: Repeats `body` and then continues from `completed`. Always bounded: the iteration cap applies whatever the kind.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: foreach walks one line of `items` per lap.

fields.name: max_iterations
fields.label: Max iterations
fields.help: 0 uses the configured ceiling.

node_kinds.title: Ask the user
node_kinds.description: Pauses the run until the user types an answer on the node.

node_kinds.title: Set variable
node_kinds.description: Writes a graph variable.

fields.name: mode
fields.label: Mode
fields.help: append joins onto what is already there, separated by a blank line - how a transcript grows across a loop.

fields.name: prefix
fields.label: Prefix
fields.help: Put in front of the appended text, e.g. a speaker's name.

node_kinds.title: Get variable
node_kinds.description: Reads a graph variable.

node_kinds.title: Print
node_kinds.description: Writes a value to the run log. The debugger's best friend.

node_kinds.title: Math
node_kinds.description: Arithmetic on two numbers. Int works in whole numbers, float keeps the fraction; text on a pin gives up its first number.

fields.name: type
fields.label: Type
fields.help: Int turns every pin into a whole number.

node_kinds.title: Compare
node_kinds.description: Compares two values: numbers as numbers, anything else as text.

node_kinds.title: Logic
node_kinds.description: AND, OR or XOR of two flags, or NOT of the first one.

node_kinds.title: Select
node_kinds.description: One of two values, picked by a condition.

node_kinds.title: Append
node_kinds.description: Joins texts end to end. Add a pin for every extra part.

fields.name: separator
fields.label: Separator
fields.help: Put between the parts. \n is a new line.

node_kinds.title: Format
node_kinds.description: Fills a template: {0}, {1}... become the inputs with that number.

fields.name: template
fields.label: Template
fields.help: Write {0}, {1}... where each input should go.

node_kinds.title: Text case
node_kinds.description: Upper case, lower case, trimmed or capitalized text.

node_kinds.title: Replace
node_kinds.description: Replaces every occurrence of one piece of text with another.

node_kinds.title: Text check
node_kinds.description: Whether text contains, starts or ends with another piece, or is empty.

node_kinds.title: Length
node_kinds.description: How many characters a text has.

node_kinds.title: Substring
node_kinds.description: A piece of text, from a start position and for a length.

fields.name: start
fields.label: Start
fields.help: Negative counts from the end.

fields.name: length
fields.label: Length
fields.help: 0 takes the rest.

node_kinds.title: Split
node_kinds.description: Cuts text at a separator into one piece per line - what a Loop's foreach walks - and counts the pieces.

fields.name: separator
fields.label: Separator
fields.help: Empty splits at spaces and new lines. \n is a new line.

node_kinds.title: To Int
node_kinds.description: A whole number from anything; text gives up the first number in it.

node_kinds.title: To Float
node_kinds.description: A number from anything; text gives up the first number in it.

node_kinds.title: To Text
node_kinds.description: Any value as text.

node_kinds.title: To Bool
node_kinds.description: true, yes, sim, on and anything but zero read as true.

node_kinds.title: Comment
node_kinds.description: A box that names a part of the graph. It never runs; moving it moves the nodes inside it.

fields.name: move_mode
fields.label: Moving it
fields.help: group carries the nodes inside along; comment moves the box alone.

professions.name: agent
professions.title: Agent
professions.description: Plain agent, no specialism. Reads, edits, runs commands and searches the web - the whole toolbox, pointed at whatever the task says. Reach for it when no profession below is the obvious fit.

professions.name: architect
professions.title: Architect
professions.description: Software architect. Reads the codebase and designs: boundaries, data flow, trade-offs, the order the work should happen in. Never edits files - it hands back a design the writers implement.

professions.name: code_writer
professions.title: Code Writer
professions.description: Implementation worker. Carries out one focused, self-contained change: reads what it needs, edits or creates files, and runs commands to verify.

professions.name: documenter
professions.title: Documenter
professions.description: Documentation writer. Reads code and writes the docs that explain it - docstrings, README sections, API references. Edits files but runs nothing.

professions.name: wiki_writer
professions.title: Wiki Writer
professions.description: Long-form writer. Produces the prose that lives outside the code: guides, architecture notes, onboarding pages, changelog entries.

professions.name: ui_designer
professions.title: Ui Designer
professions.description: Interface designer. Builds and refines the user-facing surface: layout, states, spacing, contrast, responsiveness. Edits markup and styles.

professions.name: teacher
professions.title: Teacher
professions.description: Explainer. Reads the code and teaches it: what it does, why it is built that way, what to watch out for. Never edits anything.

professions.name: tester
professions.title: Tester
professions.description: Test writer. Adds the tests a change needs and runs them, reporting what passes and what it could not cover.

professions.name: coder
professions.title: Coder
professions.description: Implementation worker. Carries out ONE focused, self-contained change: reads what it needs, edits or creates files, and runs commands to verify. Give it a precise, bounded task with clear acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended planning or work that spans many unrelated areas.

professions.name: explorer
professions.title: Explorer
professions.description: Read-only investigator. Searches and reads the workspace (and the web) to answer a focused question - locating code, tracing behavior, gathering facts. Cannot modify files or run processes. Use it to fan out research in parallel before you plan or change anything.

professions.name: reviewer
professions.title: Reviewer
professions.description: Code reviewer. Reads code and diffs and runs the review/build/test tools to judge quality, correctness, and risk, then reports findings. Read-only with respect to source: it never edits files. Use it to get an independent assessment of a change or an area of the codebase.

tools.name: analyze_logcat
tools.description: Analyse Android logcat for crashes and bugs and return a compact, structured report instead of raw log text
